title: Embroidery workers in Surat protest for wage and shift demands
seoTitle: Surat embroidery workers protest wages and shifts

tea.why: Embroidery workers are protesting over long working hours, lack of weekly holidays, and wages.
tea.want: Workers want eight-hour shifts, paid weekly holidays, minimum wages, overtime pay, and no reduction in earnings.
tea.changed: Oct 20: Labour leader Shaan Khan announced that the union will soon reveal the next phase of its ongoing agitation.

summary: Embroidery workers in Surat, Gujarat, are continuing a three-month-long agitation over working hours, wages, and weekly holidays. Workers report facing 12 to 14-hour daily shifts without adequate rest or fair compensation. Their demands include an eight-hour shift that maintains earnings comparable to current 12-hour shifts, paid weekly holidays, minimum wages, and overtime payments. Negotiations have stalled after workers rejected a monthly wage proposal from the Textile Embroidery Jobwork Association of Surat (TEJAS). Meanwhile, the Southern Gujarat Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SGCCI) stated that implementing eight-hour shifts would require half a million additional workers. The protests saw heightened tensions on October 15 when police detained between 60 and 70 workers marching toward the district collector's office. Labour representatives have also reported preliminary concerns that participating workers may be facing job dismissals.
organizers: Textile Embroidery Jobwork Association of Surat
Southern Gujarat Chamber of Commerce and Industry
demands: Earnings for eight hours comparable to twelve hours
response: Surat City Deputy Commissioner of Police Rajesh Parmar stated that workers marching to the district collector's office were detained because they had not secured the necessary permissions for the gathering.

arrests.text: Surat police detained around 60–70 workers who were heading towards the district collector’s office

updates.text: Talks between TEJAS and workers occurred, followed by a proposed monthly wage of ₹14,300 for eight hours.
Surat police detained between 60 and 70 workers attempting to march to the district collector's office.
Labour leader Shaan Khan announced that the union will soon disclose its next phase of mobilization.
